items.title: Logarithmic capacity and the two-dimensional Laplace layer kernel
items.statement:
For $x\ne y$ in $\mathbb R^2$, the logarithmic Laplace fundamental solution is $G_2(x,y)=-(2\pi)^{-1}\log|x-y|$. If $\Gamma$ is a closed piecewise-smooth curve and $\lambda$ is a smooth density, its two-dimensional single-layer trace is
$$V_\Gamma\lambda(x)=-\frac1{2\pi}\int_\Gamma\log|x-y|\lambda(y)\,ds_y.$$

For a compact set $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ with positive finite logarithmic capacity, let $\mathcal P(K)$ be the Borel probability measures supported on $K$, let $I(\mu)=\int_K\int_K\log\frac1{|x-y|}\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y)$ with value $+\infty$ on the diagonal, and define
$$I(K)=\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal P(K)} I(\mu),\qquad \operatorname{cap}(K)=e^{-I(K)}.$$
This definition fixes length units: scaling $K$ changes its capacity and adds a constant-mode term to the logarithmic layer operator, as proved separately by the homothety theorem on this page.

items.title: Bessel and Slobodeckij norms agree at order one half
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$, define
$$[f]_{1/2,2}^2=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\int_{\mathbb R^2}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^2}{|x-y|^3}\,dx\,dy.$$
There is a finite constant $c_*>0$ such that
$$[f]_{1/2,2}^2=c_*\int_{\mathbb R^2}|\xi|\,|\widehat f(\xi)|^2d\xi.$$
Consequently, the norm $\|f\|_2^2+[f]_{1/2,2}^2$ is equivalent on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ to the Bessel-potential norm $\int_{\mathbb R^2}(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}|\widehat f(\xi)|^2d\xi$. The two completions therefore define the same $H^{1/2}(\mathbb R^2)$ space with equivalent norms.

items.title: The three-dimensional Laplace Newton kernel
items.statement: For $x\ne y$ in $\mathbb R^3$, the Newton kernel is $G_3(x,y)=(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}$. Its distributional fundamental-solution property $-\Delta_xG_3(x,y)=\delta_y$ is proved in [[lem-bem-newtonian-kernel-is-fundamental-solution]]. The kernel fixes the sign and $4\pi$ normalization for every three-dimensional layer operator on this page.

items.title: Fourier transform of the three-dimensional plane Poisson kernel
items.statement:
For $t>0$ and $z\in\mathbb R^2$, let
$$P_t(z)=\frac{t}{2\pi(|z|^2+t^2)^{3/2}}.$$
Then $P_t\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ has integral one and, under the negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier convention,
$$\widehat{P_t}(\xi)=e^{-2\pi|\xi|t}\qquad(\xi\in\mathbb R^2).$$

items.title: Sound-soft exterior Helmholtz problem for a spherical obstacle
items.statement:
Fix $a>0$, $k>0$, and $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C)$. Write $S_a=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=a\}$. The sound-soft exterior Helmholtz problem is to find a complex-valued $u\in C^2(\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|>a\})$ that extends continuously to $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|\ge a\}$ and satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ for $|x|>a$, with boundary restriction $u|_{S_a}(a\omega)=f(\omega)$, and
$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\sup_{\omega\in\mathbb S^2}\left|r\bigl(\partial_r u(r\omega)-ik u(r\omega)\bigr)\right|=0.$$
The time factor is $e^{-i\omega t}$, so this is the outgoing convention. The obstacle is the closed ball $\{|x|\le a\}$; its boundary is smooth and its exterior is connected. This definition makes no claim for nonspherical obstacles or nonsmooth data.

items.title: Logarithmic capacity and single-layer scaling under homothety
items.statement:
Use the logarithmic energy and capacity conventions of [[def-bem-logarithmic-capacity-and-two-dimensional-layer-scaling]]. If $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ is compact and has $0<\operatorname{cap}(K)<\infty$ and $s>0$, then $\operatorname{cap}(sK)=s\operatorname{cap}(K)$. If $\Gamma$ is a closed piecewise-smooth curve and $\lambda$ is a smooth density, define $\Gamma_s=s\Gamma$ and $\lambda_s(sy)=s^{-1}\lambda(y)$. Then
$$V_{\Gamma_s}\lambda_s(sx)=V_\Gamma\lambda(x)-\frac{\log s}{2\pi}\int_\Gamma\lambda\,ds_y.$$
Thus changing length scale adds a constant-mode term of rank at most one (zero when $s=1$); the formula is retained separately from the three-dimensional kernel $1/(4\pi|x-y|)$.

items.title: The three-dimensional Newton kernel is a fundamental solution
items.statement:
For every $y\in\mathbb R^3$, the locally integrable kernel $G_3(x,y)=(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}$ of [[def-bem-newtonian-kernel-in-three-dimensions]] satisfies $-\Delta_xG_3(x,y)=\delta_y$ in the sense of distributions: for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}G_3(x,y)(-\Delta\varphi(x))\,dx=\varphi(y).$$

items.title: Sobolev pullback and Green identity on Lipschitz graphs
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\psi:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be $L$-Lipschitz, put $\Phi(z,t)=(z,t+\psi(z))$, and let $G=\{(z,s):s>\psi(z)\}$. Pullback by $\Phi$ and by its inverse preserves volume and is bounded on $H^1(\mathbb R^3)$. The localized pullbacks from either side of a Lipschitz graph to flat half-boxes are bounded in $H^1$. A function $u\in H^1$ up to the graph has a bounded local $L^2$ trace $\tau u$, obtained from its flattened one-dimensional endpoint trace. For compactly supported smooth $\eta$ in a graph chart,
$$\int_G\big((\partial_j u)\eta+u\partial_j\eta\big)\,dx=\int_{\partial G}(\tau u)\eta n_j\,dS.$$
Here, with derivatives defined almost everywhere,
$$dS=\sqrt{1+|\nabla\psi(z)|^2}\,dz,\qquad n\,dS=(\partial_1\psi,\partial_2\psi,-1)\,dz.$$
For a domain below the graph the normal sign reverses. These graph surface measures and normals agree on overlapping rigid graph charts, so they define an intrinsic surface measure and almost-everywhere unit outward normal on a compact Lipschitz boundary. Such a boundary satisfies $|\Gamma\cap B(x,r)|\le Cr^2$ for small $r$ and $|\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,\Gamma)<\delta\}|\le C\delta$ for small $\delta$.

Matching local traces on the two sides make piecewise $H^1$ functions glue to $H^1$ with the piecewise weak gradient. A zero-trace $H^1$ function supported inside a boundary chart extends by zero through the graph with no distributional boundary derivative; it can be approximated in $H^1$ by smooth functions supported strictly on its own side. The corresponding assertions hold after finite chart localization on a bounded Lipschitz domain or bounded boundary collar.

items.title: Lipschitz polyhedral boundary, orientation, and trace spaces
items.statement:
Assume [[def-countable-choice|Countable Choice]].

Let $\Omega^-$ be a nonempty bounded connected open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ whose boundary $\Gamma=\partial\Omega^-$ is a compact connected orientable Lipschitz surface. A **Lipschitz graph chart** is a rigid coordinate change in which $\Gamma$ is the graph $x_3=\psi(x_1,x_2)$ of a Lipschitz function on an open subset of $\mathbb R^2$, with $\Omega^-$ on one side of that graph. A **polyhedral boundary** is such a boundary made from finitely many planar polygonal faces meeting along edges and vertices; all surface-discretization claims below use this polyhedral subclass. Put $\Omega^+=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline{\Omega^-}$ and assume $\Omega^+$ is connected. For the fixed-atlas space conventions below, the boundary data include a compatible Borel surface measure $dS$ and an almost-everywhere unit outward normal $n$, with the following graph realizations and bounded positive graph area densities on every chosen chart. These compatible realizations are supplied data for the Countable-Choice space assertions, not conclusions from bare Lipschitzness under Countable Choice. Under the Axiom of Choice, [[lem-bem-lipschitz-graph-sobolev-and-green-interface]] constructs them for every compact Lipschitz boundary and proves their compatibility; the general analytical trace and layer theorems state that axiom. On polyhedral charts the data are directly the finite face areas and face normals. The normal points from $\Omega^-$ into $\Omega^+$. In a rigid chart with $\Omega^-$ above the graph $x_3=\psi(x_1,x_2)$ it is $n=(\partial_1\psi,\partial_2\psi,-1)/\sqrt{1+|\nabla\psi|^2}$ almost everywhere; reverse the sign when the domain is below the graph. Rigid coordinates transform this vector to physical coordinates. The graph surface measure is $dS=\sqrt{1+|\nabla\psi|^2}\,dx_1dx_2$. Compatibility on overlaps is part of the fixed boundary data; the cited AC graph theorem proves it for arbitrary Lipschitz charts. On a polyhedron these are the face-area measure and outward face normals.

Fix a finite Lipschitz graph atlas $\{(U_j,\psi_j)\}_{j=1}^J$, with surface parametrizations $\Phi_j(z)=(z,\psi_j(z))$ in the rigid chart coordinates, and a subordinate finite Lipschitz partition of unity $\{\chi_j\}_{j=1}^J$ whose chartwise supports have positive distance from the chart edges. On $\mathbb R^2$, use the real subspace of the real-order Bessel-potential completion in [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Its published norm uses the weight $(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$. Fix here the equivalent Hilbert norm
$$q(g)^2=\int_{\mathbb R^2}(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}|\widehat g(\xi)|^2d\xi.$$
The inequalities $(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\le(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\le2\pi(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ identify the same completion and classes under the negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier convention of [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-fractional-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Define the real space $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ by requiring every localized chart pullback $g_j=(\chi_jg)\circ\Phi_j$, extended by zero outside its chart, to belong to that Euclidean space, and fix the **square-sum chart norm**
$$\|g\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}^2=\sum_{j=1}^J q(g_j)^2.$$
Its inner product is the sum of the real weighted Fourier inner products. The following fixed-data norm and completeness assertions use only Countable Choice and the supplied compatible measure with bounded positive chart densities; they make no geometry-existence or atlas-compatibility assertion under that weaker axiom. This Hilbert norm is equivalent to the finite sum of chart norms: $(\sum_jq(g_j)^2)^{1/2}\le\sum_jq(g_j)\le\sqrt J(\sum_jq(g_j)^2)^{1/2}$. It controls $L^2(\Gamma)$, because graph surface Jacobians are bounded above and below and $g=\sum_j\chi_jg$. It is complete: a chart-norm Cauchy sequence has a global $L^2$ limit by that bound; its localized pullbacks converge in $L^2$ to the pullbacks of this limit, while completeness of each Euclidean weighted space gives convergence in each $q$ norm. The two limits agree, so the limit belongs to the defined chart space and convergence holds in the finite square sum.

Let real $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ be the continuous real dual, with its operator norm and pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_\Gamma$; the dual of this real Hilbert space is Hilbert by [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]. The interior and exterior traces of an $H^1$ function are denoted $\gamma^-u$ and $\gamma^+u$; their common chartwise trace space is $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ once the applicable trace theorem is proved. This fixed-atlas chart-space convention applies to the stated Lipschitz geometry, including its polyhedral and $C^2$ subclasses. It defines the Hilbert and dual norms; no boundary trace or lifting theorem is assumed by that convention.

The complex space is the Hilbert complexification of the real space: $\|g_1+ig_2\|^2=\|g_1\|^2+\|g_2\|^2$. Its $H^{-1/2}$ is the continuous conjugate dual, with pairing linear in the density and conjugate-linear in the trace, extending the real pairing. A complex density is a distribution via the **bilinear** test action $T_\lambda(v)=\langle\lambda,\overline v\rangle_\Gamma$. For either scalar field the continuous realization $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\subset L^2(\Gamma)\subset H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ uses $\langle f,g\rangle_\Gamma=\int_\Gamma f\overline g\,dS$ in the complex case and $\int_\Gamma fg\,dS$ in the real case. These inclusions follow from the just-proved $H^{1/2}\to L^2$ bound and Cauchy–Schwarz.

No smoothness at edges or vertices is included in this definition. The normal is only used almost everywhere. On every Lipschitz boundary use the intrinsic graph surface measure just specified, with the chart partition; on a polyhedral boundary it equals the sum of planar face-area measures. The general Lipschitz class and its $C^2$ subclass therefore use the same measure and orientation conventions.

items.title: Spherical harmonic modes are orthogonal, complete for continuous data, and have polynomial evaluation bounds
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H_\ell$ be the degree-$\ell$ spaces on $\mathbb S^2$ from [[def-three-dimensional-spherical-harmonic-space]], with surface measure of total mass $4\pi$, and let $P_\ell$ be orthogonal projection in $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$. Define $\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}$ by the polar-coordinate identity $\Delta=\partial_{rr}+2r^{-1}\partial_r+r^{-2}\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}$. Then $\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}g=-\ell(\ell+1)g$ for $g\in\mathcal H_\ell$; for all smooth $v,w$ on the sphere, $\langle v,\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}w\rangle=\langle\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}v,w\rangle$; the spaces are mutually orthogonal and their algebraic sum is uniformly dense in $C(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C)$. For smooth $f$, for every integer $m\ge1$ there is a constant $C_m(f)$ such that $\|P_\ell f\|_2\le C_m(f)(1+\ell)^{-m}$. For $g\in\mathcal H_\ell$,
$$\|g\|_\infty\le\sqrt{\frac{2\ell+1}{4\pi}}\,\|g\|_2.$$
For each integer $p\ge0$ there is $C_p$ independent of $\ell,g$ such that $\|g\|_{C^p(\mathbb S^2)}\le C_p(1+\ell)^{p+1/2}\|g\|_2$.
The angular Dirichlet form satisfies $-\langle\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}g,g\rangle=\ell(\ell+1)\|g\|_2^2$ for $g\in\mathcal H_\ell$.
For every continuous $f$, the ordered partial sums $\sum_{\ell=0}^N P_\ell f$ converge to $f$ in $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$.

items.title: Outgoing spherical Hankel modes have positive flux and no positive-real zeros
items.statement:
For real $z>0$, let $h_\ell^{(1)}$ be defined in [[def-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-functions]] and set $h_\ell^{(2)}(z)=\overline{h_\ell^{(1)}(z)}$. Then both solve the degree-$\ell$ spherical radial Helmholtz equation, are linearly independent, and
$$\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{h_\ell^{(1)}(z)}(h_\ell^{(1)})'(z)\bigr)=z^{-2}.$$
In particular, neither vanishes for $z>0$, and for $k>0$, $r>0$,
$$r^2\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)}\,\partial_r h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)\bigr)=1/k.$$

items.title: The combined-field operator for smooth-boundary Helmholtz scattering
items.statement:
Let $\Omega^-$ be a bounded connected $C^2$ domain in $\mathbb R^3$ with connected boundary $\Gamma$, let $\Omega^+=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline{\Omega^-}$ be connected, and let $n$ point outward from $\Omega^-$. Fix $k>0$ and $\eta\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. The outgoing Helmholtz kernel is
$$G_k(x,y)=\frac{e^{ik|x-y|}}{4\pi|x-y|},\qquad x\ne y.$$
For $\phi\in C^\infty(\Gamma)$ and $x\notin\Gamma$, define $S_k\phi(x)=\int_\Gamma G_k(x,y)\phi(y)\,dS_y$ and $D_k\phi(x)=\int_\Gamma\partial_{n_y}G_k(x,y)\phi(y)\,dS_y$. The **combined-field potential** is $u_\phi=D_k\phi-i\eta S_k\phi$, and its exterior trace defines the smooth-density operator $A_{k,\eta}\phi=\gamma^+u_\phi$. This definition makes no assertion that $A_{k,\eta}$ extends boundedly or Fredholmly to a Sobolev space; these analytical properties are proved in separate theorems. For this smooth-boundary branch, $\gamma^+$ denotes the trace from $\Omega^+$ and uses the same fixed normal $n$ as the interior trace. For this $C^2$ surface, fix a finite graph atlas and subordinate partition as in the general Lipschitz chart-space convention of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], using graph surface measure. Use its square-sum Hilbert norm, real spaces, complexification and conjugate-dual convention for $H^{\pm1/2}(\Gamma)$. This imports the space convention only; the $C^2$ trace/lift and layer theorems are proved separately and do not invoke the polyhedral trace theorem.

items.title: The chart and chordal surface H1/2 norms are equivalent
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ and the chartwise norm on $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ be as in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]. For a measurable $g$ define
$$\|g\|_{H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{ch}}(\Gamma)}^2=\|g\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}^2+\int_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|^2}{|x-y|^3}\,ds_xds_y.$$
There are constants $c,C>0$ depending only on the fixed finite atlas and partition such that, first for smooth $g$ and then by completion,
$$c\|g\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}\le\|g\|_{H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{ch}}(\Gamma)}\le C\|g\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}.$$

items.title: The H1 trace and lifting theorem on a compact Lipschitz boundary
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $\Gamma$ be any compact Lipschitz boundary in the geometry of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]; no polyhedral restriction is imposed. The interior trace $\gamma^-:H^1(\Omega^-)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded. On every bounded exterior boundary collar $C=\Omega^+\cap U$, where $U$ is a bounded neighborhood of $\Gamma$ with Lipschitz collar boundary, the exterior trace $\gamma^+:H^1(C)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded. The corresponding localized assertion holds over each boundary chart. Thus an exterior function has this trace whenever it is $H^1$ up to the boundary on such collars; membership in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega^+)$ alone does not assert a boundary trace. There is a bounded linear right inverse $L:H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\to H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ with $\gamma(Lg)=g$. There is also a bounded extension operator $E:H^1(\Omega^-)\to H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ with $(Eu)|_{\Omega^-}=u$.

Let $\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ denote the completion of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ in the norm $\|u\|_{\dot H^1}=\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}$. Its elements have an $L^6$ representative, the trace $\gamma:\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is bounded, and the right inverse above may be chosen with compact support near $\Gamma$.

items.title: Shape-regular surface meshes and conforming P0 densities
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a polyhedral boundary as in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]. A **conforming surface triangulation** $\mathcal T_h$ is a finite collection of nondegenerate closed planar triangles covering $\Gamma$, with disjoint relative interiors, such that two distinct triangles meet only in a common full edge, a common vertex, or not at all. For $T\in\mathcal T_h$, write $h_T=\operatorname{diam}(T)$ and let $\rho_T$ be the radius of the largest disk contained in $T$; the family is **shape regular** if $\sup_{h,T}h_T/\rho_T<\infty$, and **quasi-uniform** if $\inf_{h,T}h_T/h>0$ for $h=\max_{T\in\mathcal T_h}h_T$.

The conforming **P0 density space** is $X_h=\{\lambda_h\in L^2(\Gamma):\lambda_h|_T\text{ is constant for every }T\in\mathcal T_h\}$. The continuous inclusion $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\hookrightarrow L^2(\Gamma)$ follows because each chart Bessel norm controls its L2 norm and the fixed partition is finite. Hence every $\lambda_h$ defines a bounded functional $v\mapsto\int_\Gamma\lambda_hv$ on $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$; thus $X_h\subset H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$. This inclusion makes the single-layer Galerkin method conforming in its energy space.

items.title: Every outgoing spherical Helmholtz mode is an outgoing Hankel mode
items.statement: Let $u$ be a classical solution of $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ for $r>a$, where $k>0$, and satisfy the outgoing condition in [[def-pe18-exterior-helmholtz-problem]]. For each $\ell$, its orthogonal projection $u_\ell(r,\cdot)$ onto $\mathcal H_\ell$ has the form $u_\ell(r,\cdot)=c_\ell h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)$ with a fixed vector $c_\ell\in\mathcal H_\ell$. Before imposing outgoingness, every degree-$\ell$ coefficient is a linear combination of $h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)$ and $h_\ell^{(2)}(kr)=\overline{h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)}$. This statement is modewise; it does not assert convergence of the partial-wave series as $r\to\infty$.

items.title: The Helmholtz single-layer and double-layer traces have the Laplace jump signs
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma=\partial\Omega^-$ be the connected closed $C^2$ surface from [[def-bem-smooth-helmholtz-combined-field-operator]], with outward normal $n$. For $k>0$ and smooth densities $\lambda,\phi$, the Helmholtz layers in that definition satisfy
$$\gamma^-S_k\lambda=\gamma^+S_k\lambda,\qquad \partial_n^-S_k\lambda-\partial_n^+S_k\lambda=\lambda,$$
$$\gamma^-D_k\phi-\gamma^+D_k\phi=-\phi.$$
The one-sided conormal limits in the single-layer formula and trace limits in the double-layer formula are taken along the fixed normal $n$. The double-layer conormal jump is not asserted in this item.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For the $C^2$ boundary and orientation of [[def-bem-smooth-helmholtz-combined-field-operator]], there are bounded traces from either side of a bounded collar into $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, bounded trace lifts into $H^1(\Omega^-)$ and into compactly supported $H^1(\mathbb R^3)$, and bounded extensions of the classical layers
$$S_k:H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)\longrightarrow H^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R^3),\qquad D_k:H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\longrightarrow H^1(\Omega^-)\oplus H^1_{\rm loc}(\overline{\Omega^+}).$$
Here the exterior local space means $H^1$ on each bounded exterior collar/domain truncation, including its boundary. Both restrictions solve $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ weakly and have bounded weak conormals in $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$. With the fixed normal $n$, they obey Green's identity, with duality linear in the conormal and conjugate-linear in the trace. Their exterior restrictions are smooth away from $\Gamma$ and satisfy the uniform Sommerfeld condition $\sup_\omega|r(\partial_r-ik)u(r\omega)|\to0$. Bounds are at fixed $k$ and fixed bounded neighborhoods. The single layer has one trace across $\Gamma$.

items.title: Exterior finite-energy functions have a trace controlled by their gradient
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For the connected exterior domain $\Omega^+$ of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], let
$$E^+(\Omega^+)=\{u\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega^+):u\in L^6(\Omega^+),\ \nabla u\in L^2(\Omega^+)\}.$$
There is a constant $C$ depending only on $\Omega^-$ and its fixed trace atlas such that every $u\in E^+(\Omega^+)$ has $\gamma^+u\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and
$$\|\gamma^+u\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}\le C\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(\Omega^+)}.$$

items.title: Weak Laplace single-layer potentials and energy spaces
items.statement:
Write $G_3$ for the Newton kernel of [[def-bem-newtonian-kernel-in-three-dimensions]]. For a smooth density $\lambda$ on $\Gamma$, the classical single-layer potential is
$$S\lambda(x)=\int_\Gamma G_3(x,y)\lambda(y)\,dS_y,\qquad x\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\Gamma.$$

Let $\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ in the norm $\|u\|_{\dot H^1}=\|
abla u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$, using its $L^6$ representative and the trace from [[lem-bem-lipschitz-trace-and-lifting]]. For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, consider the equation for $u\in\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}
abla u\cdot
abla v\,dx=\langle\lambda,\gamma vangle_\Gamma\qquad(v\in\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)).$$
Call such a function a weak single-layer potential and write $S\lambda=u$ when it exists. Define the exterior energy space $E^+(\Omega^+)=\{u\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega^+):u\in L^6(\Omega^+),\ 
abla u\in L^2(\Omega^+)\}$. For a weakly harmonic function $u^-\in H^1(\Omega^-)$, define its weak outward conormal by $\langle\partial_n^-u^-,gangle=\int_{\Omega^-}
abla u^-\cdot
abla L^-g$, where $L^-g$ is any $H^1$ trace lift. For a harmonic $u^+\in E^+(\Omega^+)$, use the same fixed normal $n$ by $\langle\partial_n^+u^+,gangle=-\int_{\Omega^+}
abla u^+\cdot
abla L^+g$ for a compactly supported local lift. In either case the value is independent of the lift: the difference of two lifts has zero trace, and weak harmonicity makes its gradient pairing zero. The exterior formula also gives $\int_{\Omega^+}
abla u^+\cdot
abla v^+=-\langle\partial_n^+u^+,\gamma^+v^+angle$ for every $v^+\in E^+(\Omega^+)$. Indeed, subtract a compactly supported lift of $\gamma^+v^+$; the remaining zero-trace finite-energy function is approximated in gradient norm by compactly supported zero-trace functions using radial cutoffs: $\|v^+
abla\chi_R\|_2\le C\|v^+\|_{L^6(\{R<|x|<2R\})}	o0$. Boundary-chart flattening, zero extension, inward translation, and convolution approximate each zero-trace cutoff by interior smooth tests, so weak harmonicity makes its gradient pairing zero. This proves the energy identity without a flux assumption at infinity. Existence, uniqueness, agreement with the displayed kernel for smooth densities, and the conormal jump are proved in [[thm-bem-single-layer-transmission-mapping-and-coercivity]]. The weak definition fixes the normalization at infinity through $u\in L^6(\mathbb R^3)$; arbitrary additive constants are excluded.

items.title: P0 averages approximate smooth densities in H negative one half
items.statement:
Let $\{\mathcal T_h\}$ be a shape-regular family of conforming surface triangulations of $\Gamma$ from [[def-bem-surface-mesh-and-piecewise-constant-density-space]], and let $h=\max_{T\in\mathcal T_h}h_T$. For $v\in L^1(\Gamma)$ define the element-average projection
$$\Pi_hv|_T=|T|^{-1}\int_Tv\,ds.$$
There is a family-independent constant $C$ such that
$$\|v-\Pi_hv\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}\le Ch^{1/2}\|v\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}\qquad(v\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)).$$
If $\lambda$ is continuously differentiable on each planar face (with facewise derivatives square integrable), then
$$\|\lambda-\Pi_h\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}\le Ch^{3/2}\|\nabla_\Gamma\lambda\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}.$$
Here $\nabla_\Gamma\lambda$ is the ordinary two-dimensional gradient on each planar face; no continuity of these derivatives across edges is assumed.

items.title: A positive far-panel quadrature residual and normalized cluster combination
items.statement:
Let $T,S$ be disjoint nondegenerate compact triangles in a conforming surface mesh, let $d$ be supplied with $0<d\le\operatorname{dist}(T,S)$, and set
$$A_{TS}=\frac1{4\pi}\int_T\int_S\frac{1}{|x-y|}\,dS_y\,dS_x.$$
Apply $m_T$ and $m_S$ successive midpoint refinements to $T$ and $S$, respectively. The resulting subtriangles have maximum diameters $h_T=2^{-m_T}\operatorname{diam}(T)$ and $h_S=2^{-m_S}\operatorname{diam}(S)$. Give each subtriangle its area as a positive weight and its centroid as its node, obtaining rules $(x_i,w_i)$ and $(y_j,v_j)$. Then
$$B_{TS}=\sum_i\sum_j\frac{w_iv_j}{4\pi|x_i-y_j|}$$
satisfies
$$|A_{TS}-B_{TS}|\le\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm quad}:=\frac{|T||S|(h_T+h_S)}{4\pi d^2}.$$
Repeated midpoint subdivision makes this residual tend to zero. For exact algebraic panel coordinates, a supplied strict algebraic lower bound for $d$ and outward interval evaluation therefore gives an effective certificate at every positive tolerance; for other coordinates the corresponding certified separation and arithmetic bounds are required.

For the physical kernel, if the source nodes have charges $q_j=v_j/(4\pi)$ in $B(c,a)$ and the target nodes lie in $B(d_c,b)$ with $R=|d_c-c|>a+b$, then the literal single-cluster evaluator of [[alg-three-dimensional-laplace-cluster-expansion]] has $Q=\sum_j|q_j|$ and target-weight sum $W_T=\sum_iw_i$. Its contribution to the entry error is at most
$$W_T\frac{Q}{R-b}\frac{(a/(R-b))^{p+1}}{1-a/(R-b)}.$$
Add separately certified quadrature, node-evaluation and outward-arithmetic radii. This is a single-cluster estimate, not a multilevel or global complexity result.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. On the $C^2$ surface of [[def-bem-smooth-helmholtz-combined-field-operator]], the extensions of [[lem-bem-smooth-trace-and-helmholtz-layer-extension]] satisfy, for $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$,
$$\gamma^-D_k\phi-\gamma^+D_k\phi=-\phi,\qquad \partial_n^-D_k\phi-\partial_n^+D_k\phi=0,$$
$$\gamma^-S_k\lambda-\gamma^+S_k\lambda=0,\qquad \partial_n^-S_k\lambda-\partial_n^+S_k\lambda=\lambda.$$
Trace and conormal equalities hold in $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, respectively; both conormals use the same normal $n$ pointing out of $\Omega^-$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the $C^2$ geometry of [[def-bem-smooth-helmholtz-combined-field-operator]]. For each fixed $k>0$ and real $\eta\ne0$, its operator extends boundedly to complex $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and
$$A_{k,\eta}=\tfrac12I+K_k-i\eta V_k,\qquad V_k=\gamma S_k,$$
where both $K_k$ and the restriction $V_k:H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ are compact. Thus $2A_{k,\eta}=I-\mathcal K_{k,\eta}$ with compact $\mathcal K_{k,\eta}=-2K_k+2i\eta V_k$. No uniform estimate in $k$ is asserted.

items.title: The finite-energy double-layer transmission space
items.statement:
Use the exterior energy space $E^+(\Omega^+)$ and weak conormal conventions of [[def-bem-laplace-layer-potentials-and-energy-spaces]]. For $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ let
$$\mathcal A_\phi=\{(u^-,u^+)\in H^1(\Omega^-)\times E^+(\Omega^+):\gamma^-u^- -\gamma^+u^+=-\phi\}.$$
When it exists uniquely, denote by $D\phi$ the pair in $\mathcal A_\phi$ minimizing
$$\mathcal E(u^-,u^+)=\int_{\Omega^-}|\nabla u^-|^2dx+\int_{\Omega^+}|\nabla u^+|^2dx.$$
Existence, uniqueness, harmonicity, and equality of the weak conormals are proved in [[thm-bem-double-layer-transmission-jumps-and-bounds]].

For $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $x\notin\Gamma$, the corresponding classical potential, whose agreement with the minimizer is proved in [[thm-bem-double-layer-transmission-jumps-and-bounds]], is $D\phi(x)=\int_\Gamma\partial_{n_y}G_3(x,y)\phi(y)\,dS_y$. The sign in the imposed jump, $\gamma^-D\phi-\gamma^+D\phi=-\phi$, is the convention for this kernel.

items.title: The three-dimensional single layer is bounded and coercive
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, with $\Gamma$ as in [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], there is a unique $u=S\lambda\in\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfying the weak single-layer equation of [[def-bem-laplace-layer-potentials-and-energy-spaces]]. It is harmonic on $\Omega^-$ and $\Omega^+$, its two traces agree, and its weak conormal traces satisfy
$$\partial_n^-u-\partial_n^+u=\lambda\quad\hbox{in }H^{-1/2}(\Gamma).$$
The trace operator $V\lambda:=\gamma u$ maps $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ boundedly into $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, and there are constants $C,c>0$ depending on $\Gamma$ such that
$$\|u\|_{\dot H^1}+\|V\lambda\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}},\qquad \langle\lambda,V\lambda\rangle_\Gamma\ge c\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}}^2.$$
If $\lambda\in L^\infty(\Gamma)$ (in particular for facewise smooth densities reaching edges or discontinuous P0 densities), this weak potential agrees away from $\Gamma$ with $\int_\Gamma(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}\lambda(y)dS_y$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, and the polyhedral geometry and normal $n$ of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]]. Let $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and let $(u^-,u^+)\in H^1(\Omega^-)\times E^+(\Omega^+)$ satisfy
$$\gamma^-u^- -\gamma^+u^+=-\phi,$$
$$\int_{\Omega^-}\nabla u^-\cdot\nabla v+\int_{\Omega^+}\nabla u^+\cdot\nabla v=0\qquad(v\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)).$$
Then, with smooth representatives off $\Gamma$,
$$u^\pm(x)=\int_\Gamma\partial_{n_y}G_3(x,y)\phi(y)\,dS_y,\qquad x\in\Omega^\pm.$$
The integral is absolutely convergent for each $x\notin\Gamma$, and equality holds without any vanishing condition at edges or vertices.

If additionally the restriction of $\phi$ to each closed face extends to a $C^1$ function on a planar neighborhood of that face, define, at a face-interior point $x$,
$$K_{\rm ker}\phi(x)=\int_\Gamma\partial_{n_y}G_3(x,y)\phi(y)\,dS_y.$$
This integral is absolutely convergent (the same-face integrand is zero away from $y=x$), and the interior/exterior normal limits are $K_{\rm ker}\phi(x)\mp\phi(x)/2$. Thus their Sobolev trace average agrees almost everywhere with $K_{\rm ker}\phi$; equivalently this is its principal-value realization. All assertions about values at edges and vertices themselves remain Sobolev trace assertions, not a pointwise half-jump formula there. In particular the statement includes facewise smooth densities agreeing across shared edges and taking nonzero values there.

items.title: The double-layer potential has the stated jumps and bounds
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the affine class $\mathcal A_\phi$ in [[def-bem-double-layer-transmission-space]] has a unique minimum-energy pair $D\phi=(u^-,u^+)$. It is harmonic on both sides, satisfies
$$\gamma^-D\phi-\gamma^+D\phi=-\phi,\qquad \partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi,$$
and obeys
$$\|\nabla u^-\|_{L^2(\Omega^-)}+\|\nabla u^+\|_{L^2(\Omega^+)}\le C\|\phi\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}.$$
Consequently the average trace $K\phi=(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi)/2$ is in $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and the common conormal $q_\phi=\partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi$ is in $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, with both maps bounded. For every $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the weak potential agrees away from $\Gamma$, with smooth representatives, with the absolutely convergent integral $\int_\Gamma\partial_{n_y}G_3(x,y)\phi(y)dS_y$. No vanishing condition at polyhedral edges or vertices is required.

items.title: Calderon boundary operators and trace conventions
items.statement:
For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ define the Laplace Calderon boundary operators by
$$V\lambda=\gamma S\lambda,\qquad K\phi=\tfrac12(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi),$$
$$K'\lambda=\tfrac12(\partial_n^-S\lambda+\partial_n^+S\lambda),\qquad W\phi=-\partial_n^-D\phi=-\partial_n^+D\phi.$$
Here $\gamma S\lambda$ is the common trace, conormal traces use the orientation of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], and the last equality is meaningful because the weak double layer has a common conormal derivative. This page uses the real duality pairing between $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. The well-definedness and bounded mapping properties of $V,K,K',W$ are proved in [[thm-bem-calderon-mapping-and-jump-identities]].

items.title: P0 Galerkin BEM for the single layer is well posed and quasioptimal
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Gamma$ be as above, let $\mathcal T_h$ be any finite conforming surface triangulation, and let $X_h$ be its P0 space. For every $f\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ there are unique $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\lambda_h\in X_h$ satisfying
$$\langle\mu,V\lambda\rangle_\Gamma=\langle\mu,f\rangle_\Gamma\quad(\mu\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)),\qquad \langle\mu_h,V\lambda_h\rangle_\Gamma=\langle\mu_h,f\rangle_\Gamma\quad(\mu_h\in X_h).$$
For constants $c,C>0$ from [[thm-bem-single-layer-transmission-mapping-and-coercivity]],
$$\|\lambda-\lambda_h\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}\le(1+C/c)\inf_{\mu_h\in X_h}\|\lambda-\mu_h\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}.$$
The method is conforming because $X_h\subset H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$; this is an exact Galerkin estimate and contains no quadrature or geometry error.

items.title: Bounded invertibility of the smooth-boundary Helmholtz combined field
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, let $k>0$ and real $\eta\ne0$, and use the smooth-boundary geometry, spaces and operator $A_{k,\eta}$ of [[def-bem-smooth-helmholtz-combined-field-operator]]. Then $A_{k,\eta}$ extends to a bounded bijection on complex $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ with bounded inverse. In particular, for this fixed $k,\eta$ there is a finite constant $C_{k,\eta}=\|A_{k,\eta}^{-1}\|$ such that
$$\|\phi\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}\le C_{k,\eta}\|A_{k,\eta}\phi\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}.$$
The constant can also depend on $\Gamma$; no bound uniform as $k$ varies is asserted. For every boundary datum $f\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, $u=D_kA_{k,\eta}^{-1}f-i\eta S_kA_{k,\eta}^{-1}f$ is the unique outgoing weak exterior Dirichlet solution with trace $f$ in the local $H^1$ class of [[thm-bem-exterior-helmholtz-dirichlet-uniqueness]].

items.title: Bounded Calderon maps and signed jump identities
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, as in the single- and double-layer transmission theorems. For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the operators in [[def-bem-calderon-boundary-operators]] are bounded as
$$V:H^{-1/2}\to H^{1/2},\quad K:H^{1/2}\to H^{1/2},\quad K':H^{-1/2}\to H^{-1/2},\quad W:H^{1/2}\to H^{-1/2}.$$
Their weak traces satisfy
$$\gamma^-S\lambda=\gamma^+S\lambda=V\lambda,\qquad \partial_n^-S\lambda=K'\lambda+\tfrac12\lambda,\quad \partial_n^+S\lambda=K'\lambda-\tfrac12\lambda,$$
$$\gamma^-D\phi=K\phi-\tfrac12\phi,\qquad \gamma^+D\phi=K\phi+\tfrac12\phi,\qquad \partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi=-W\phi.$$
All equalities are in the stated Sobolev trace or dual spaces and use the outward normal orientation fixed on the A page.

items.title: Certified touching-panel and disjoint-panel quadrature for the Laplace P0 matrix
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, and let $T,S$ be panels of the conforming surface triangulation in [[def-bem-surface-mesh-and-piecewise-constant-density-space]]. For $x\ne y$ put $G_3(x,y)=(4\pi|x-y|)^{-1}$ and define
$$\mathcal I_{TS}=\int_T\int_SG_3(x,y)\,dS_y\,dS_x.$$
The integral is absolutely convergent. If $V$ is the single-layer operator of [[def-bem-calderon-boundary-operators]], then
$$\mathcal I_{TS}=\langle1_T,V1_S\rangle_\Gamma.$$

For coincident panels, panels sharing a full edge, and panels sharing a vertex, the exact affine parameter integral for $\mathcal I_{TS}$ has a finite decomposition into integrals
$$c_m\int_R q_m(z)\,dz,\qquad R=\{(x,y):0\le y\le x\le1\},$$
where $c_m>0$, each $q_m$ is smooth on a neighborhood of $R$, and every integral is the Duffy-transformed case with exponent $\alpha=0<2$. The decomposition includes every singular-face dimension: in each four-simplex of the finite decomposition the zero face may have dimension $0$, $1$, or $2$. If $T$ and $S$ are disjoint, their positive separation instead gives one smooth reference-triangle integral with the same exponent $\alpha=0$.

The constructions supply explicit lower bounds for every denominator and explicit derivative bounds for every required amplitude. Given exact algebraic panel coordinates and any positive absolute tolerance $\varepsilon$, the finite nested Gaussian procedure described in the proof terminates with an outward-certified value $\widetilde{\mathcal I}_{TS}$ satisfying $|\mathcal I_{TS}-\widetilde{\mathcal I}_{TS}|\le\varepsilon$. For other coordinate representations, the procedure has the same guarantee when certified finite incidence, nondegeneracy, separation, and arithmetic bounds are supplied as input. It makes no termination claim for deciding incidences from an uncertified arbitrary-real oracle.

items.title: The hypersingular operator is elliptic modulo constants
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $W:H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\to H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ be the hypersingular operator of [[def-bem-calderon-boundary-operators]]. It is symmetric and nonnegative, its kernel is exactly the constants, and there is $c>0$ such that
$$\langle W\phi,\phi\rangle_\Gamma\ge c\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\|\phi-a\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}^2.$$
The real scalar $m_\Gamma(\phi):=\int_\Gamma\phi\,dS$ is the $L^2$ integral, not a pairing of two elements of $H^{1/2}$. The continuous embeddings $H^{1/2}\subset L^2\subset H^{-1/2}$ use the fixed Hilbert chart convention; the second map sends $f$ to the functional $g\mapsto\int_\Gamma fg\,dS$. Thus $m_\Gamma(\phi)$ can equivalently be evaluated by pairing this realized negative-order functional with $1$. The stabilized form
$$b(\phi,\psi)=\langle W\phi,\psi\rangle_\Gamma+m_\Gamma(\phi)m_\Gamma(\psi)$$
is bounded and coercive on $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. Consequently, for each $f\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ there is a unique $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ such that $b(\phi,\psi)=\langle f,\psi\rangle_\Gamma$ for every $\psi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$.

items.title: Certified near-quadrature and far-multipole matrix assembly
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T_h$ and $X_h$ be the surface mesh and P0 space from [[def-bem-surface-mesh-and-piecewise-constant-density-space]]. For an ordered target/source pair $(T,S)$ define its exact 3D Laplace single-layer matrix entry by
$$A_{TS}=\langle1_T,V1_S\rangle_\Gamma=\int_T\int_S\frac{1}{4\pi|x-y|}\,dS_y\,dS_x,$$
where the equality is proved for every panel pair by [[lem-bem-panel-pair-duffy-certificates]]. Supply a positive per-entry tolerance $\tau_{TS}$ and construct exactly one auditable certificate as follows.

Process the finite set of ordered panel pairs once in lexicographic mesh order. For each pair, first certify whether the panels coincide, share an edge, share a vertex, or are disjoint; if the incidence is unresolved, return **uncertified**. Use exact algebraic panel coordinates or provide the needed certified incidence, separation (for disjoint panels), denominator, and derivative bounds, together with outward arithmetic whose radii can be refined to zero. A missing required bound returns **uncertified**. After selecting a standard branch below, refine its quadrature and arithmetic certificates by levels $k=0,1,2,\ldots$ and accept the first level whose total error bound is at most $\tau_{TS}$. At each level refine precision until the combined node-value, evaluation and outward-arithmetic contribution to the entry bound is at most $2^{-k-1}\tau_{TS}$; charge the fiber-quadrature remainder separately.

- **Near certificate.** For coincident panels or panels sharing an edge or vertex, use the finite sign-cell/pulling-simplex identity of [[lem-bem-panel-pair-duffy-certificates]]. A disjoint pair may also use that lemma's smooth fallback whenever the whole-panel far-cluster condition below is unavailable. Each term is a reference-triangle integral $\int_R|z|^{-\alpha_m}q_m(z)dz$ with $\alpha_m<2$ and transformed amplitude $G_m\in C^{2n}([0,1]^2)$. Record the exact change-of-variables derivation, the supplied derivative bounds, and the positive Gaussian remainder $E_m$ from [[cor-duffy-weighted-product-gauss-error]]. If $\rho_m$ is the separately certified total of nested fiber, node-value and outward arithmetic radii, require $\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm near}=\sum_m|c_m|(E_m+\rho_m)\le\tau_{TS}$. A custom near identity may be accepted as a supplied finite certificate only after its identity, derivative bounds, every Gaussian hypothesis, and total error at most $\tau_{TS}$ have been verified; otherwise return **uncertified**. Do not run the standard refinement loop on a custom identity. For the standard panel-pair construction, every final exponent is $\alpha_m=0$.

- **Far certificate.** For disjoint panels, fix certified balls containing the entire source and target panels. Choose positive centroid rules on finite midpoint subdivisions and use [[lem-bem-far-panel-quadrature-residual]] to record the physical-kernel quadrature residual $\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm quad}$ and any separate outward evaluation radius $\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm eval}$. If the source nodes with physical charges $q_j=v_j/(4\pi)$ lie in $B(c,a)$ and the target nodes lie in $B(d,b)$ with the strict condition $R=|d-c|>a+b$, evaluate the single-cluster field of [[alg-three-dimensional-laplace-cluster-expansion]]. For $Q=\sum_j|q_j|$ and target weight sum $W_T$, record
$$\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm far}=\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm quad}+\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm eval}+W_T\frac{Q}{R-b}\frac{(a/(R-b))^{p+1}}{1-a/(R-b)}+\varepsilon_{TS}^{\rm FMM-arith}.$$
The final term is the outward arithmetic radius of the finite cluster evaluation; it is zero only for an exact-arithmetic evaluation. At level $k$, use $m_T=m_S=p=k$ and refine outward precision as needed. If the whole-panel balls fail $R>a+b$, do not use this tail and instead use the disjoint smooth near fallback with $n=1$, subdividing both reference triangles at level $k$. No global multilevel or $O(N)$ work claim is made.

For a touching pair, use the standard identity and take $n=1$ in the weighted product rule on each similar-triangle subdivision at level $k$; when the opposite face has dimension three use $2^k$ midpoint subintervals for the finite fiber integral. Use midpoint subdivision, so each reference-triangle diameter is $2^{-k}$ times its original diameter, and use the per-level precision budget above. If a custom identity or any required hypothesis cannot be verified, return **uncertified**.

For every pair require its certified total error $\varepsilon_{TS}\le\tau_{TS}$. Given one successful certificate for every ordered pair, form $\widetilde A_h=(\widetilde A_{TS})$. If $\gamma_h>0$ is a certified lower norm bound satisfying
$$\|c\|_2\le\gamma_h^{-1}\left\|\sum_Tc_T1_T\right\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)},$$
compute the returned defect certificate
$$\delta_h=\gamma_h^{-2}\left(\sum_{T,S}\varepsilon_{TS}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
Any missing or unverified panel-pair geometry, identity, derivative bound, arithmetic radius or certificate returns **uncertified** and no matrix-defect claim. If no valid $\gamma_h$ is supplied, return the assembled matrix and its entrywise certificates without a matrix-defect bound. In particular, the batch-26 Duffy rule alone does not certify arbitrary coincident or edge-adjacent pairs.

items.title: A certified matrix defect transfers to a Galerkin error bound
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space and $X_h\subset H$ a finite-dimensional subspace. Let $a:H\times H\to\mathbb R$ be bounded with continuity constant $C$ and coercive with constant $c>0$, and let $F\in H'$. Write $F_h=F|_{X_h}$ and
$$\|F_h\|_{X_h'}=\sup_{\substack{w_h\in X_h\\\|w_h\|_H\le1}}|F_h(w_h)|.$$
Let $u\in H$ solve $a(u,w)=F(w)$ for all $w\in H$, and let $u_h\in X_h$ be its exact Galerkin solution. Suppose a bilinear form $\widetilde a_h:X_h\times X_h\to\mathbb R$ and load $\widetilde F_h\in X_h'$ satisfy
$$|\widetilde a_h(v_h,w_h)-a(v_h,w_h)|\le\delta\|v_h\|_H\|w_h\|_H,\qquad |\widetilde F_h(w_h)-F_h(w_h)|\le\eta\|w_h\|_H$$
for all $v_h,w_h\in X_h$, with $0\le\delta<c$. The perturbed equation $\widetilde a_h(\widetilde u_h,w_h)=\widetilde F_h(w_h)$ has a unique solution and
$$\|u-\widetilde u_h\|_H\le(1+C/c)\inf_{v_h\in X_h}\|u-v_h\|_H+\frac1c\left(\eta+\frac{\delta(\|F_h\|_{X_h'}+\eta)}{c-\delta}\right).$$
Independently of the condition $\delta<c$ in the variational estimate, for a successful assembly in [[alg-bem-certified-inexact-matrix-assembly]], every near or far certificate gives $|A_{TS}-\widetilde A_{TS}|\le\varepsilon_{TS}\le\tau_{TS}$. If the supplied $\gamma_h>0$ satisfies $\|c\|_2\le\gamma_h^{-1}\|\sum_Tc_T1_T\|_{H^{-1/2}}$, then the returned value
$$\delta_h=\gamma_h^{-2}\left(\sum_{T,S}\varepsilon_{TS}^2\right)^{1/2}$$
bounds the bilinear form defect in the fixed $H^{-1/2}$ norm. This guarantee includes the exact near-pair identities and all derivative, nested-fiber, evaluation and arithmetic errors, and uses the far tail only under $R>a+b$; an uncertified output supplies no such bound.

For the standard branches of [[alg-bem-certified-inexact-matrix-assembly]], assume the required geometry, derivative and denominator certificates are verified and outward arithmetic can reach each prescribed positive radius. Every positive entry tolerance is then attained after finitely many levels. A supplied custom identity is accepted only with an already verified finite certificate meeting its tolerance; no refinement-termination assertion is made for arbitrary custom identities.

For P0 single-layer BEM, take $H=H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ with its Sobolev norm and $a(v,w)=\langle w,Vv\rangle_\Gamma$. The single-layer theorem supplies $c,C$, and a successful matrix-assembly certificate supplies $\delta$.

title: Boundary-integral equations and Galerkin BEM — Examples

items.title: A constant density on the sphere gives a constant trace
items.statement:
For $R>0$, let $S_R=\{y\in\mathbb R^3:|y|=R\}$ and take density $\lambda=1$. The classical Newton single-layer potential is
$$S1(x)=\int_{S_R}\frac{1}{4\pi|x-y|}\,dS_y=\begin{cases}R,&|x|\le R,\\ R^2/|x|,&|x|\ge R.\end{cases}$$
It is continuous on $S_R$ with trace $R$. With outward radial normal, the interior and exterior normal derivatives at the sphere are $0$ and $-1$, respectively, so their difference is $1$, the density.

items.title: A unit sphere checks both layer jump signs
items.statement: On the unit sphere $S_1$ with outward normal, let both layer densities be the constant $1$. The single layer has boundary trace $1$ and conormal jump $\partial_n^-S1-\partial_n^+S1=1$. The double-layer kernel $\partial_{n_y}G_3$ has potential $-1$ in the unit ball and $0$ outside; hence $\gamma^-D1-\gamma^+D1=-1$. Its common normal derivative is zero. Thus these conventions agree with $\gamma^-D-\gamma^+D=-\phi$ and $\partial_n^-S-\partial_n^+S=\lambda$.

items.title: The logarithmic single layer on a circle changes by a scale term of rank at most one
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma=S_1$ be the unit circle, let $s>0$, and scale the curve to $S_s$. For a smooth density $\lambda$ on $S_1$, set $\lambda_s(sy)=s^{-1}\lambda(y)$. Then
$$\operatorname{cap}(S_s)=s\operatorname{cap}(S_1),\qquad V_{S_s}\lambda_s(sx)=V_{S_1}\lambda(x)-\frac{\log s}{2\pi}\int_{S_1}\lambda\,ds.$$
In particular, the change in the layer trace depends only on the total charge, so it has rank at most one (rank zero for $s=1$ and rank one otherwise). For $\lambda=1/(2\pi)$ on $S_1$ and $s=e$, the total charge is one and the trace changes by $-1/(2\pi)$.

items.title: A reentrant polyhedral edge has an H1 harmonic singularity
items.statement:
At a straight reentrant edge with cross-sectional opening angle $\omega\in(\pi,2\pi)$, put $\alpha=\pi/\omega\in(1/2,1)$ and in local cylindrical coordinates define
$$u(r,\theta,z)=r^\alpha\sin(\alpha\theta),\qquad 0<r<r_0,\quad0<\theta<\omega,\quad |z|<z_0.$$
Then $u$ is harmonic in the wedge, has zero trace on its two planar side faces, belongs to $H^1$ locally up to the edge, and does not belong to $H^2$ in any neighborhood of the edge.

items.title: A two-by-two inexact assembly ledger
items.statement:
Use Euclidean norm on $X=\mathbb R^2$ and exact matrix/load
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad f=\binom10.$$
Approximate it by
$$\widetilde A=A+E,\qquad E=\begin{pmatrix}1/100&0\\0&-1/100\end{pmatrix},\qquad \widetilde f=f.$$
The exact coercivity and continuity constants are $c=1$ and $C=3$. The defect matrix is $E=\operatorname{diag}(1/100,-1/100)$, so $\|E\|_2=1/100<1/50$; take the conservative certified $\delta=1/50$, load defect $\eta=0$, and $\|F_h\|=1$. The perturbed solve is
$$\widetilde u=\binom{19900/29999}{-10000/29999},$$
while $u=(2/3,-1/3)$. The transfer theorem gives the certified error $\|u-\widetilde u\|_2\le1/49$; the exact rational difference is also smaller than $1/49$.

This is a finite algebraic error ledger illustrating how a certified assembly defect enters the perturbation theorem; it does not assert that this particular matrix is a panel matrix from a specified mesh.
